svg.text: Whether an abandoned landfill is controlled depends on its size, not its era
a state agency prioritising legacy site remediation
whether to screen legacy sites by closure era or by
era predicts whether a site is controlled better
share with a gas system, by size
If you want more abandoned landfills controlled, the target is small ones: 338 closed sites hold under 500,000 tons each and 8% of them collect gas, in every decade equally.
Observed minus size-predicted, by decade of closure: -4%, +3%, +4%, -3% from the 1990s on. The 1990s trough is the Subtitle D wave, which closed thousands of very small dumps.
1,048 closed landfills with both a stock and a closure year. Sites closing before 1960 are drawn on the bottom row; the decade marginal starts at 1960 where the counts allow it.
